Team — forwarding Lytix's redlines. Key asks from them: stronger notice timelines, IP cap carve-out or higher cap for IP, explicit OSS carve-out, and clarity around duty to defend. Procurement needs answers before their April pricing window closes.

My suggested approach for the call:
- Offer 30-day notice + cure for third-party claims where cure is possible; for claims where we elect defense we want timely notice + cooperation language.
- For IP infringement: propose uncapped indemnity for copyright/trademark/software misappropriation, but propose a 2x annual contract cap for patent claims OR escalate to execs for carve-out.
- OSS carve-out: we can exclude claims arising from customer modifications and list standard OSS provenance exceptions.
- Defense costs: Redwood will provide and control initial defense with right to approve counsel; if either side reasonably objects we can discuss counsel selection procedures.

Lauren — can you draft a clean counterproposal for the MSA redlines that captures that approach? Kar­thik — pls align on what pricing/credit trade we can offer if Lytix insists on uncapped patent indemnity.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa / Karthik — drafting notes below and attached a proposed clause set (clean and tracked). High-level:

1) Notice & Cure
- Accept 30-day written notice where cure is commercially reasonable; clarify that failure to timely notify does not relieve Redwood of indemnity but may affect mitigation of damages.

2) IP indemnity carve-outs + caps
- Copyright/trademark/software copying: Redwood will indemnify and defend; cap = 2x annual committed spend for the contract year (we can justify based on unit economics).
- Patent claims: Redwood will indemnify for third-party patent claims only up to a separate patent sub-cap equal to 4x monthly committed spend, unless escalated to execs for a carve-out (we can present exec-level risk acceptance).
- OSS: carve out claims that arise solely from (a) Customer's modifications of OSS, (b) Customer's combination of OSS with other non-Redwood components where claim arises from that combination.

3) Duty to defend / control of counsel
- Redwood to have initial control of defense with obligation to keep Customer reasonably informed; Customer may engage separate counsel at its own expense if it reasonably believes there is a material conflict.

4) Cooperation and mitigation
- Standard cooperation obligations; Redwood to reimburse reasonable expenses; include an evidence-preservation clause.

Attached: MSA_Indemnity_Counter_20270404.docx (tracked changes).

If you want, I can prepare two short scripts for the call (one for sales/execs and one for procurement/legal) to keep the conversation focused.

Lauren Bishop

Alice — attaching our proposed counter language and a one-page executive summary of trade options. Quick summary of the main points:

- 30-day notice & cure for third-party claims where cure is commercially reasonable.
- Copyright/trademark/software misappropriation: Redwood indemnifies and defends; cap = 2x annual committed spend.
- Patent claims: limited indemnity with a separate higher sub-cap (4x monthly committed spend) — if Lytix requires uncapped patent exposure we will need an exec-level risk acceptance and a pricing uplift or escrow arrangement.
- OSS carve-out: claims arising solely from Customer modifications or third-party combinations are excluded.
- Redwood controls initial defense but will keep Lytix informed; Customer can replace counsel at its own cost if conflict arises.

Proposed next steps: 30-minute legal-to-legal call mid-week to go clause-by-clause and a parallel procurement call to discuss trade (credit or annual commit uplift). Kar­thik to follow up on pricing options.

Attachments: MSA_Indemnity_Counter_20270405.docx, Indemnity_Trade_Options_1pager.pdf

Best,
Marissa

Marissa / Lauren — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear summary. Procurement is comfortable with the notice/cure language. Legal has two remaining asks before we can proceed to procurement sign-off:

1) Patent carve-out: Lytix cannot accept a patent indemnity sub-cap without board-level sign-off on our side for strategic product lines. We are open to executing a limited-term pilot with the proposed sub-cap (6 months) followed by re-evaluation, or an escrow/insurance-backed arrangement.

2) Evidence & audit rights: we need a short clause ensuring Redwood will preserve relevant logs and provide a timely account of any KV/prefix caching behavior that is relevant to liability determination (we're trying to nail down the data we would need to assess alleged infringement).

If you can confirm those two points (pilot/escrow for patent risk; preservation/audit clause) we can move this to procurement and aim for signature by April 20. Also, please attach SOC2 Type II evidence and your indemnity claims runbook (if available).

Attachments requested: SOC2_Report_Link, Claims_Runbook (if available)
